page: Microsoft Azure M96bs_v3 is an x86_64 architecture server belonging to the MBSMediumMemoryv3 family, running on the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor. It features 96 dedicated vCPUs mapped from 48 physical Intel Xeon 8473C cores with hyper-threading enabled at 2.0 threads per core. The processor operates at a base frequency of 4.0 GHz and includes 105 MB of L3 cache. The system is equipped with 768.0 GB of system memory, providing a resource density of 8.0 GB of RAM per vCPU. There is no local storage bundled with this instance, though it is premium storage capable and optimized for block storage performance. No hardware GPU accelerators are present.

In benchmark evaluations, the M96bs_v3 demonstrates strong multi-threaded capabilities and high memory throughput. Memory bandwidth tests place both cached small-block reads and uncached large-block reads and writes in the top 10% tier. Multi-core CPU performance is rated as strong in stress-ng and top-tier in PassMark and Geekbench suites. Single-core performance is more moderate, placing in the middle 50% for stress-ng single-core tests, though Geekbench single-core results reach the top 10% tier. Database operations and static web serving throughput both rank in the top 10% tier, while Redis SET operations achieve 114.5 million operations per second, placing in the top 25% tier. For machine learning workloads, LLM inference speeds for prompt processing are strong across small, medium, and large models, though text generation speeds fall into the average range.

The primary hardware tradeoff of the M96bs_v3 is the complete absence of local storage, requiring reliance on external block storage. From a qualitative cost-efficiency perspective, the high density of dedicated compute resources and top-tier memory bandwidth offset the premium associated with large-scale memory allocations. This profile is suited for memory-intensive and multi-threaded workloads. Appropriate applications include large-scale database operations, memory-cached web serving, multi-threaded data decompression, and CPU-based LLM prompt processing.
